A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same research, with v3 explicitly identifying itself as an extension of the earlier work. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v2 includes Appendices A–E; v3 incorporates selected appendix material into the main text but contains no appended supplement, despite referring to one.

before.justification: v2 reports original depth-estimation, reconstruction, ablation and robotic-grasping results, including additional experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds sparse-depth completion, prompting-strategy and SfM-based reconstruction evaluations.

M1.justification: v3 retains the original convolutional decoder fusion and adds a distinct pattern-agnostic mechanism in Section III-D. Valid depth points become tokens, join image tokens in self-attention with UV positional encoding, and enhance image features through a zero-initialized residual projection before decoding. The completion variant also introduces median-based depth normalization.

E1.justification: v3 adds sparse-point completion evaluation on NYUv2, ScanNet, DIODE, ETH3D and KITTI, plus a new completion setting on Waymo, which already appeared in v2. DTU and Replica introduce SfM-prompted multi-view reconstruction. Completion training also adds reported datasets including VKITTI2, UrbanSyn and DynamicReplica. This substantially extends the original coverage beyond low-resolution LiDAR prompting.

E2.justification: Table III adds evaluated completion comparators Marigold-DC, Omni-DC and PriorDepthAny.; BP-Net matches the existing BPNet baseline. Tables IV–V introduce reconstruction comparisons including Murre, IGEV-MVS, COLMAP and MonoSDF. Conversely, the Depth Anything v1 row in v2's ARKitScenes Table 1 is absent from v3's corresponding Table II, although the prose still names it.

E3.justification: New completion evaluations use 1,500 randomly selected sensor-depth points and report same-machine runtime comparisons. The HyperSim strategy comparison uses 30×40 depth maps versus 1,200 random points. New reconstruction evaluations use Detector-free SfM prompts and TSDF, with three-view DTU comparisons and Chamfer-distance reporting. The stated original ARKitScenes/ScanNet++ splits and training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table VII adds a cross-setting comparison of the two prompting strategies on HyperSim. Conversely, several appendix-only analyses are absent from the supplied v3, including resolution sensitivity, Zip-NeRF frame-resampling effects, fusion combined with ControlNet, and RANSAC-versus-polyfit findings. The original main ablations remain, and the Depth Pro replacement experiment moves from v2 Table 5 into v3 Table VI.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental results. The new tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables III–V and VII add substantial completion, reconstruction and strategy-comparison results. For example, v3 reports average DTU Chamfer distance of 1.02 mm versus Murre's 1.42 mm, and Replica F-score of 0.90 versus 0.85. These are new evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v2. Retained ARKitScenes, ScanNet++, grasping and original ablation values are unchanged; some appendix results and the ARKitScenes Depth Anything v1 row are omitted.

T1.justification: The DPT preliminaries and edge-aware loss equations retain their mathematical content. The new prompting mechanism is described algorithmically without new theoretical propositions or proofs. Omission of v2's standard metric-formula tables removes explanatory detail rather than establishing changed metric definitions.

C1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction expand the contribution from low-cost LiDAR prompting to pattern-agnostic sparse-point prompting. v3 claims state-of-the-art performance on eight zero-shot depth benchmarks and adds a principal claim of superior SfM-prompted MVS reconstruction without further fine-tuning. The original 4K, data-pipeline and robotic-application claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly identifies irregular sparse-depth patterns as a limitation of map-based prompting and explains token serialization as the mechanism for broader applicability. It interprets Table VII as showing complementary strengths: the original strategy favors upsampling, while the new strategy handles completion better. SfM results motivate reconstruction using only monocular-depth training. Existing long-range LiDAR and temporal-flickering limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new normalization and SfM workflow, adds completion runtime information, and explicitly reports public code with a repository address. However, substantial v2 appendix documentation is absent: dataset-specific losses, frame-selection rules and Zip-NeRF processing cost, TSDF voxel size, RANSAC implementation, vehicle-LiDAR preprocessing, and robotic hardware/data/model details. These are documentation changes, not evidence that retained experiments changed procedures.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions itself relative to its CVPR 2025 predecessor and expands its relationship to recent completion and SfM-guided reconstruction research. Related work adds substantive descriptions of approaches including Pixel-Perfect Depth, Depth Anything 3, InfiniDepth, SHARP and LingBot-Depth. Murre, previously cited in v2, becomes a central reconstruction comparator and source of evaluation settings.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and reframed as an extension, with revised authorship, abstract and contribution structure. The experimental narrative now distinguishes upsampling, completion and SfM reconstruction. Selected appendix material is integrated into implementation and analysis sections, while the Appendix A–E structure is not carried over. This is substantial structural revision despite extensive retention of original prose.

P2.justification: v3 adopts journal-style typography and table captions, adds the prompting diagram in Figure 4, completion and reconstruction comparisons in Figures 7–8, and four new experimental tables. Original figures and tables are redistributed, and the Depth Pro appendix table is merged into Table VI. v2's appendix Figures 9–16 and metric-definition tables are absent.

improvement.justification: The new strategy comparison and SfM evaluations provide substantive evidence for broader applicability. However, the supplied v3 omits substantial reproducibility information and supplementary checks present in v2. Its blanket accuracy-superiority claims also exceed Table III: Marigold-DC has lower Waymo errors, and PriorDepthAny. has lower ETH3D AbsRel. The stronger methodological evidence and losses in reproducibility and claim precision coexist without a reliably clear net improvement in overall quality.
